transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. I’ll be trying to do something, and one saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, or even just a thought about another job pops in, and I’m off track. Then before I know it, the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Did you have this kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?

Yes. Even in grade school, before I was 12, it was the same kind of thing. Teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but careless. I’d lose homework, forget instructions, or just be staring out the window instead of finishing my work.
Does this trouble focusing happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yes, it’s definitely both. At work it’s caused real problems—mistakes, delays, having to redo things on jobs. I’ve lost commissions over it, and the crew doesn’t really trust me as much with scheduling or ordering anymore.

And at home, my husband’s had to take over the bills and keep track of reminders, because I’ll misplace papers or just miss what needs to be done. It’s not just one place.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I don’t think so. I get frustrated and worn out by all of this, but I wouldn’t say I feel depressed most days.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?
I’m not sure. I mean, I worry when something’s actually going wrong, but I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying all the time for no reason.
Did your trouble focusing start after a very stressful or traumatic event?

No, it didn’t start after anything traumatic. It’s been around since I was a kid. Even in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my mom I was bright but careless—losing homework, forgetting instructions, staring out the window instead of getting my work done.
